strengths: Principled and general formulation: Formulating the VLM critic via the log-odds difference of binary 'Yes/No' classification logits ($z_{\text{yes}} - z_{\text{no}}$) over a structured dual query (content match and geometric plausibility) is simple, mathematically clean, and avoids complex multi-token text generation during backpropagation.

Cross-paradigm applicability: The authors convincingly demonstrate that the VLM critic can be applied both as an auxiliary reward for score distillation sampling (SDS) pipelines and as a test-time guidance gradient during the iterative sampling loop of native 3D feed-forward diffusion models (Hunyuan3D-2.1).

Technical engineering of differentiable VLM pathways: Resolving the detachment issues commonly present in standard VLM image preprocessors (by re-engineering operations to pure Torch tensors) enables true end-to-end gradient backpropagation from multi-view renderings through the VLM back to 3D parameters/latents.

Strong qualitative and quantitative results: The method clearly reduces prominent 3D artifacts (e.g., multi-face Janus problems, disconnected geometry, missing fine-grained prompt attributes) and demonstrates consistent quantitative gains across GPTEval3D, native 3D geometry metrics (Chamfer/Hausdorff), and point-cloud foundation models (ULIP, Uni3D).
Thorough ablation studies: The paper provides meaningful analyses regarding prompt phrasing, multi-view vs. single-view VLM inputs, guidance annealing schedules, and VLM-only optimization.
weaknesses: Substantial computational and memory overhead: Backpropagating through a 7B visual-language model requires considerable GPU resources (~49–53 GB VRAM on an NVIDIA A100), doubling the generation time of feed-forward models (from 60s to 120s) and limiting real-time usability on consumer-grade hardware.

Small test sample size for feed-forward benchmark: The quantitative evaluation for feed-forward models (Table 2) is conducted on only 24 prompts, which is a relatively narrow sample compared to standard benchmarks and limits statistical power.

Heuristic prompt sensitivity: The effectiveness of the critic relies heavily on hand-crafted prompt phrasing (as shown in Appendix B and Table 4); the paper does not systematically explore how sensitive the gradient signal is to prompt rephrasing or language variations across different domains.

strengths: Unifying perspective across 3D paradigms: The paper successfully demonstrates that a vision-language model (VLM) can act as an effective, differentiable semantic and spatial critic in both optimization-based (SDS) and feed-forward native 3D diffusion (test-time guidance) pipelines.

Simple yet effective formulation: Deriving the critic signal via the binary log-odds difference (z_yes - z_no) from a structured dual-query prompt (checking both content match and geometric quality) provides a well-behaved scalar reward that backpropagates cleanly to 3D parameters or latents.

Key engineering contribution to differentiability: The authors identify and fix an important practical bottleneck in off-the-shelf VLMs—namely, image preprocessors detaching gradients via NumPy conversions—by re-engineering an end-to-end tensor-based pipeline to enable gradient backpropagation through the visual backbone.

Comprehensive empirical validation: Strong quantitative and qualitative improvements over competitive baselines on the GPTEval3D benchmark, external 3D-native metrics (ULIP, Uni3D), and solid ablation studies validating the dual-query prompt design, multi-view inputs, and guidance scheduling.
weaknesses: Computational overhead and memory footprint: Backpropagating gradients through a 7B-parameter VLM and differentiable rasterizers incurs significant computational cost (~49–53 GB GPU memory on an A100, taking 2.2 hours for optimization and doubling feed-forward sampling time from 60s to 120s), which limits deployment in real-time or resource-constrained settings.

Small test set for the feed-forward evaluation: While the optimization pipeline is evaluated on 110 GPTEval3D prompts, the quantitative evaluation for the feed-forward test-time guidance module in Table 2 is conducted on only 24 prompts, which weakens the statistical significance of the reported feed-forward gains.

Heuristic sensitivity of VLM prompt formulation: The critic's effectiveness relies heavily on handcrafted negative failure mode prompts (e.g., explicitly naming 'Janus-faced issue', 'broken surfaces', 'intersecting geometry'). As shown in Appendix B, performance degrades markedly with alternative wordings, suggesting potential brittleness across diverse object categories or unanticipated artifacts.

strengths: Unified framework across paradigms: The paper proposes a clean formulation that leverages pre-trained vision-language models (VLMs) as differentiable critics via binary log-odds (zyes - zno), successfully adapting the method to both optimization-based score distillation sampling (SDS) and test-time guidance (TTG) in native feed-forward 3D diffusion models.

Dual-query prompt design: The integration of both semantic alignment and explicit multi-view geometric quality criteria within the VLM prompt is well-motivated, and the ablation experiments demonstrate the utility of jointly enforcing both aspects.

Comprehensive qualitative demonstrations: The paper includes extensive visual examples across varied scenarios (fine-grained semantics, multi-object relationships, prompt perturbations) illustrating noticeable improvements over baseline methods.

Practical engineering effort: The authors identify and address a real-world bottleneck in differentiating through off-the-shelf VLMs by re-engineering image preprocessors from NumPy-detaching routines into fully tensorized PyTorch operations.
weaknesses: Small sample size for feed-forward evaluation: The quantitative assessment of the feed-forward test-time guidance module (Table 2) is conducted on only 24 prompts. This sample size is too limited to draw statistically reliable conclusions about generalizability across diverse 3D concepts.

Reliance on LLM/VLM evaluator without human study: The primary quantitative results in Table 1 rely entirely on GPT-4o-mini pairwise ratings via GPTEval3D. Since the method directly optimizes rendered views against a VLM critic (Qwen2.5-VL), evaluating primarily via another VLM introduces potential evaluation bias toward VLM-favored visual cues. A rigorous, blind user study is needed to validate perceptual quality.

Lack of analysis on gradient stability and reward hacking: Backpropagating gradients through a 7B-parameter multimodal transformer over thousands of iterations is prone to gradient vanishing/exploding, high variance, and adversarial texture artifacts (reward hacking). The paper provides minimal analysis or visualization of the gradient field ∇_X rVLM and does not clarify whether gradients are clipped, normalized, or computed at every single optimization step.

Substantial computational and memory overhead: Optimization requires ~49 GB VRAM and feed-forward guidance consumes ~53 GB VRAM on an A100 GPU (doubling the inference latency from 60s to 120s). The practical scalability and trade-offs of this heavy computational footprint are not sufficiently addressed.

Missing operational details regarding multi-view prompting: The paper does not clearly specify how the N multi-view images are structured and inputted into the VLM (e.g., whether they are passed as concatenated image tokens, a tiled multi-view mosaic, or processed sequentially), nor does it specify the exact camera sampling strategy and number of views N used during training.

strengths: Compelling and timely core motivation: repurposing modern, spatial-aware large Vision-Language Models (VLMs) as differentiable critics to resolve common semantic and geometric failure modes in 3D generation.
Broad applicability demonstrated across two distinct 3D paradigms: optimization-based score distillation sampling (SDS) and test-time guidance for native 3D feed-forward diffusion samplers.
Convincing qualitative results (e.g., Figures 1, 3, 4, and 5) illustrating improved multi-object composition, fine-grained attribute binding, and reduction of disconnected/floating artifacts.

Informative ablation analysis in Section 5.3 and Figure 6 confirming that both the multi-view input formulation and explicit geometric queries are necessary to suppress Janus and surface fracture artifacts.
weaknesses: Severe methodological and evidential issue in Table 2: Section 5.2 explicitly notes that FID, CLIP-FID, CLIP-D, and Geometry score are computed 'on all cases shown in Fig. 1 and 4' (a total of roughly 4 prompts). Reporting distribution-level statistical metrics such as FID on a handful of cherry-picked qualitative samples is mathematically invalid and uninformative.

Critical implementation details missing for feed-forward test-time guidance: Equation (10) relies on computing gradients with respect to intermediate diffusion latents $\nabla_{z_t} r_{\text{VLM}}$. In native 3D diffusion models like Hunyuan3D, mapping noisy latent $z_t$ to multi-view rendered images requires estimating $\hat{z}_0$, decoding via the 3D decoder, and differentiable rendering. The paper does not specify how this chain is implemented, whether Tweedie's formula is applied, which differentiable renderer is employed, or how memory/compute overhead is handled during the 50 diffusion steps.

Vague definition of evaluation metrics: The 'Geo.' (Geometry) score in Table 2 is neither formally defined nor explained (it is unclear whether this is a heuristic mesh check, a VLM score, or a user study).

Missing analysis of adversarial gradient exploitation: Direct optimization against frozen vision encoders / VLMs frequently induces high-frequency adversarial textures that inflate log-odds without genuine quality gains. The manuscript does not discuss gradient regularizations or investigate whether the VLM critic is vulnerable to such visual artifacts.

Presentation and bibliography defects: Duplicate references exist (e.g., [2] and [3] both cite the Qwen2.5-VL technical report; [43] and [44] cite the exact same GPTEval3D paper), alongside typos such as 'guidace' in Section 4.3.2.

strengths: The paper addresses two core bottlenecks in text-to-3D generation: fine-grained semantic misalignment and geometric inconsistencies (such as part assembly failures and the Janus problem).
The proposed dual-query formulation is intuitive and clean, structuring the VLM query to simultaneously evaluate semantic correspondence and geometric validity via log-odds backpropagation.

The framework demonstrates versatility by applying the same VLM critic concept across two major paradigms: optimization-based score distillation sampling (SDS) and test-time guidance for native 3D feed-forward diffusion models.
Ablation studies (Fig. 5 and Fig. 6) effectively demonstrate the necessity of multi-view inputs and the explicit geometric consistency query in mitigating multi-face artifacts.
weaknesses: Severe statistical flaw in Table 2 evaluation: The authors state that Table 2 evaluates metrics (including FID and CLIP-FID) 'on all cases shown in Fig. 1 and 4'. Computing distribution-level metrics like FID and CLIP-FID over a handful of qualitative examples (4-5 prompts) is mathematically invalid and provides no statistically reliable measure of generation fidelity.

Lack of essential implementation details for feed-forward guidance: In Section 4.3.2, test-time guidance computes gradients $\nabla_{z_t} r_{\text{VLM}}$ from latents $z_t$ via 'differentiable rendering of the current prediction'. For native 3D diffusion models like Hunyuan3D operating in 3D DiT latent spaces, the manuscript fails to describe how backpropagation through the 3D VAE/decoder and the renderer is performed, how many camera viewpoints $N$ are rendered per step, or how memory constraints are managed when running backward passes through a 7B VLM at every denoising step.

Vulnerability of VLM gradients and lack of adversarial analysis: Directly optimizing 3D/image representations via raw logits of large multimodal autoregressive models is known to suffer from high-frequency gradient noise and adversarial gaming. The paper does not analyze gradient stability or discuss whether smoothing or regularizers are required to prevent visual artifacts.

Evaluation lacks human user studies: GPTEval3D relies purely on GPT-4o-mini automated ratings across 110 prompts. Given that the method optimizes against a VLM critic, automated LLM/VLM evaluation is prone to correlated bias. A rigorous blind human preference evaluation is needed to validate claims of superior quality.

Visible drafting issues and duplicate references: Multiple duplicate references are present with apparent raw notes left in the bibliography (e.g., [2] and [3] are identical entries for Qwen2.5-VL with an explanatory note appended; [28] and [29] are identical CLIP entries; [43] and [44] are identical GPTEval3D entries; [26] and [42] retain leftover note annotations).

strengths: The paper tackles two well-recognized failure modes in text-to-3D generation: fine-grained semantic misalignment and spatial/geometric incoherence (such as floating components and Janus artifacts).
Formulating the VLM critic via binary log-odds (r_VLM = z_yes - z_no) over a structured dual query (content match and geometric quality) is conceptually clean and directly differentiable.
The approach is demonstrated across two distinct paradigms: optimization-based generation (SDS) and test-time guidance within native 3D feed-forward diffusion models.

The qualitative comparisons and ablations (Figures 5 and 6) provide intuitive evidence that incorporating multi-view inputs and explicit geometric prompts helps mitigate multi-face artifacts and part disconnections.
weaknesses: Fundamental evaluation flaw in Table 2: The authors state in Section 5.2 that they evaluate CLIP-D, FID, CLIP-FID, and a 'Geometry score' on 'all cases shown in Fig. 1 and 4'—which corresponds to only 4 prompt instances. Computing distribution metrics such as FID and CLIP-FID on such an extremely small sample set is statistically invalid. Furthermore, the 'Geometry score' (Geo.) is never defined or cited.

Missing critical mathematical and implementation details for feed-forward test-time guidance (Eq. 10): In native 3D diffusion (Hunyuan3D), latents z_t are noisy. The manuscript does not explain how rendered images are obtained at intermediate timestep t (e.g., whether a Tweedie one-step denoising estimate z_0 is computed, how the latents are decoded into explicit geometry, and whether the native 3D decoder is differentiable).

Computational feasibility concerns: The paper reports a total runtime of 60 seconds for 50 sampling steps of Hunyuan3D test-time guidance on a single A100 GPU. Performing 50 forward and backward passes through a 7B parameter multimodal model (Qwen2.5-VL) across multiple rendered views within 60 seconds is unusually fast; the paper omits details regarding precision, gradient checkpointing, token lengths, or rendering resolution that would verify reproducibility.

Evaluator bias and lack of human study in Table 1: Quantitative evaluation on GPTEval3D relies solely on automated pairwise rankings from GPT-4o-mini. Because the method directly optimizes multi-view renderings using a VLM objective, it is susceptible to model/evaluator alignment bias. A user study with human raters is necessary to validate these gains.

Absence of guidance baselines in the test-time guidance setting: The evaluation compares VLM3D guidance only against unguided baselines (CLAY and Hunyuan3D). To demonstrate that the VLM dual-query critic is uniquely advantageous, the paper should compare against standard test-time guidance baselines, such as CLIP-based guidance or single-query guidance.

Presentation and reference errors: The bibliography contains exact duplicate entries (e.g., [2] and [3] for Qwen2.5-VL, and [43] and [44] for GPTEval3D), and Figure 4 contains redundant and misaligned text labels.
